summary: Nez Perce NF R-6 cab built 1960 on a summit used since the 1920s; hike-in in the Frank Church Wilderness, staffed in summer, NHLR-registered 1997.

access.note: Hike-in only, deep in the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness. The cab is staffed in summer.

visit.trail_note: Hike-in only, inside the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness

events.note: Log cabin with cupola, the earlier structure on the summit. Replaced in 1960.
R-6 cab on a short base, replacing the 1928 cupola cabin. Base height is reported as 7, 8 or 10 feet depending on source.
Known-staff list places Doris and Bert Babcock in the 1960s and 1970s. Year shown is the start of the decade.

Recorder Herald item (October 16, 1975), quoted by Forest Lookouts: Salmon National Forest to furnish a radio for installation at the lookout, to link with Butte Point lookout or direct to the North Fork river patrol.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on August 25, 1997.

corrections.proposed: 1960 built (R-6 cab); 1928 is the log cupola cabin it replaced
corrections.why: NHLR and Firelookout date the current R-6 cab to 1960. The 1928 date belongs to the earlier cupola cabin.

corrections.proposed: remove (no overall height in any source)
corrections.why: No source gives an overall height. The sources give a 7 to 10 foot concrete or cinder block base, and 3.0 m is about 10 feet, which matches a base rather than the lookout.

corrections.proposed: single R-6 cab on a short base
corrections.why: The sources describe one R-6 cab on a 7 to 10 foot base. None describes a two-story building.

That page is for a different Sheep Hill in the Clearwater National Forest at 5,676 ft, listed as Gone. It is not the Nez Perce tower in this record, so its Gone status must not be applied here. The Idaho page for this tower is the one without the -2 suffix.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Keeping Watch lists 'Built: 1928' for the R-6 cab. NHLR, Firelookout and the Idaho page date the R-6 cab to 1960 and the cupola cabin to 1928. The story uses 1960 for the R-6 cab.
NHLR gives 7 feet, the Forest Lookouts history page gives 8 feet of cinder block, and Firelookout and the Idaho page give 10 feet of concrete. Not resolved; the story reports the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Brief record was wrong in four places (see corrections): the 1928 build date belongs to the earlier cabin, height_m 3.0 is a base height, kind two_story is unsupported, and the sheep-hill-lookout-2 Idaho page is about a different Sheep Hill (Clearwater NF, Gone). The Idaho page used here is the Nez Perce one without the -2 suffix. Staffing dates are undated. The 1960s Babcock entries are decades, not exact years. No fire history found in the pages read. Budget used: 6 distinct page reads, 2 searches.
